title: Pressure Injury Prevention Assessment
description: A patient is at risk of developing a pressure injury due to limited mobility. In this scenario, learners will assess the patient's condition, identify pressure injury risks, and apply appropriate prevention techniques following healthcare safety practices.
learningObjective: Learners will be able to identify pressure injury risk factors, perform skin assessments, implement prevention strategies, and demonstrate proper patient repositioning and care techniques.
topicsAddressed: Pressure injury prevention, skin assessment, patient positioning, risk assessment, patient safety, infection prevention
additionalEquipment: Hospital bed, patient care manikin, gloves, assessment sheet, repositioning aids, pillows, pressure-relieving devices
optionalEquipment:
Equipment/Supplies
Barrier cream, wound prevention documentation forms, pressure monitoring tools
setupNotes: Place the patient manikin on the hospital bed in a position requiring assessment. Ensure required equipment is available. Configure the scenario to simulate a patient with limited mobility and increased risk of pressure injury.

studentBriefing.purpose: This simulation is designed to provide learners with hands-on experience in identifying pressure injury risks and applying prevention strategies. Learners will practice patient assessment, repositioning techniques, skin care management, and communication skills required to maintain patient safety and prevent pressure-related injuries.
studentBriefing.learningObjectives:
Identify common risk factors associated with pressure injuries.
Perform a basic skin assessment to identify areas at risk.
Demonstrate proper patient repositioning techniques.
Apply pressure injury prevention measures using appropriate equipment.
Communicate patient condition and care recommendations using the SBAR framework.
Document assessment findings and preventive interventions accurately.

sbar.situation: The patient is at increased risk of developing a pressure injury due to limited mobility and prolonged periods of bed rest. A skin assessment is required, and preventive interventions need to be implemented.
sbar.background: The patient has reduced mobility and requires assistance with repositioning. The patient has been spending extended time in bed and needs ongoing monitoring to prevent skin breakdown.
sbar.assessment: The patient shows risk factors for pressure injury development, including limited movement and pressure exposure on high-risk areas such as the sacrum, heels, and elbows. Preventive measures should be initiated.
sbar.recommendation: Continue regular skin assessments, reposition the patient according to care guidelines, use pressure-relieving equipment, maintain proper skin hygiene, and document all preventive actions taken. Escalate any signs of skin breakdown to the healthcare team.

actions.title: Immediate Management
actions.prompt: The patient is identified as being at risk of developing a pressure injury due to limited mobility. What is the most appropriate immediate action the healthcare provider should take?
items: Reposition the patient and implement pressure-relieving measures such as pillows or support devices.
Leave the patient in the current position and reassess the skin condition after several hours.
Apply medication immediately without assessing the patient's skin condition.
Encourage the patient to remain still to avoid further discomfort.
actions.correct: Reposition the patient and implement pressure-relieving measures such as pillows or support devices.

actions.title: Pressure Injury Prevention Intervention
actions.prompt: Describe the steps you would take to prevent pressure injury development in this patient. Include assessment, repositioning, skin care, and communication actions.

concepts.description: Performs a skin assessment and identifies high-risk pressure areas (sacrum, heels, elbows, and other bony prominences).
Explains the importance of repositioning the patient regularly to reduce prolonged pressure.
Identifies the need for pressure-relieving devices such as pillows, cushions, or specialized mattresses.
Mentions maintaining skin hygiene, keeping skin clean and dry, and monitoring for signs of breakdown.
Communicates findings and preventive care actions using appropriate healthcare documentation or SBAR handoff.

actions.resultName: would assess the patient's skin for redness or breakdown, reposition the patient regularly, use pillows or pressure-relieving devices to reduce pressure on bony areas, maintain proper skin hygiene, and report any changes to the healthcare team

actions.title: Pressure Injury Prevention Care Sequence
actions.prompt: Arrange the following nursing care interventions in the correct order to prevent pressure injuries in a patient with limited mobility.
items: Assess the patient's skin condition and identify areas at risk for pressure injury.
Explain the repositioning plan to the patient and provide necessary assistance.
Reposition the patient using proper techniques to relieve pressure on vulnerable areas.
Apply pressure-relieving devices such as pillows, cushions, or support surfaces.
Document the assessment findings, interventions performed, and communicate any concerns to the healthcare team.
